task: Fix the broken webhook signature verification after the HMAC key was rotated.

candidate_memories.content: Webhook endpoint returns 401 for all incoming webhooks since the HMAC key was rotated on the partner side.
The HMAC key must be updated in secrets/webhook_signing.yaml with the new key provided by the partner.
The partner sent the new key by secure email on May 10; it was received but not yet applied.
The old key expired on May 15 when the partner completed their key rotation.
Session 3 note: the payments team reported all incoming webhooks returning 401 unauthorized errors.
The webhook endpoint receives payment events from the partner at a rate of 500 per minute.
Session 7 note: the security team audited all webhook endpoints for signature verification coverage.
Old practice: webhook secrets were stored in environment variables before secrets management was adopted.
The secrets manager rotates credentials automatically for internal services but not for partner-managed keys.
Session 12 note: the integration team added webhook retry logic with exponential backoff.
Old webhook guide: the HMAC key was rotated annually on a fixed schedule before the partner moved to event-driven rotation.
Partner-managed key rotations must be tracked in a calendar to ensure timely updates.
Session 4 note: the monitoring team added a webhook verification failure rate alert.
Failed webhooks are retried up to 3 times before being moved to the dead-letter queue.
Session 9 note: the partner integration team added a sandbox environment for testing webhooks.
The webhook signing key is a 256-bit random secret used for HMAC-SHA256 verification.
HMAC key updates must be applied before the partner completes their rotation to avoid a verification gap.
Session 6 note: the partner provided documentation for their key rotation procedures.
Old secrets guide: webhook secrets were stored alongside the SMTP credentials in the secrets file.
The webhook endpoint enforces a 5-second processing timeout per event.
